newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hang Seng Bank sees profit strain.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hang Seng Bank sees profit strain.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Bank expects to achieve growth in operating profit in the second half of calendar 1996 but the increase might not be as great as that achieved in the first half, vice chairman and chief executive Alexander Au said on Tuesday.

"We did mention in the (first half) results announcement that margins are under pressure because of very keen competition and therefore probably the second half will see banking profits come under a bit of strain," Au told Reuters.
"I think there will still be growth, but then we think growth will probably be less spectactular than the first half."
Speaking after attending a Hong Kong Trade Development Council promotion, Au said the second half pressure applied to other Hong Kong-based banks as well.

He said Hang Seng's first half operating profit rose about 25 percent and preferred this measure than net profitability as the latter included profits on the sale of investments which helped boost the bottom line by 34 percent to HK$4.35 billion.

"To grow significantly higher from an already high base will not be easy," Au said, adding that it was difficult to predict calendar 1996 net profit, which analysts expect will show a rise of about 13 percent from 1995's HK$7.98 billion.
